source.author: verg
source.text: Primus ab aetherio venit Saturnus Olympo, arma Iovis fugiens et regnis exsul ademptis.
source.text_original: Primus ab aetherio venit Saturnus Olympo, / arma Iovis fugiens et regnis exsul ademptis.
source.text_english: First came Saturn from ethereal Olympus, fleeing Jupiter’s arms and banished from the kingdom he had lost.

reuse.author: lact
reuse.text: sed postquam Saturnus a filio pulsus in Latiumque delatus est arma Iouis fugiens et regnis exul ademptis, cum iam populus uel noui regis metu uel sua sponte depranatus deum colere desisset regemque pro deo habere coepisset, cum ipse propemodum parricida exemplo ceteris esset ad uiolandam pietatem, deseruit propere terras iustissima uirgo, sed non, ut ait Cicero, et Iouis in regno caelique in parte resedit .
reuse.text_original: sed postquam Saturnus a filio pulsus in Latiumque delatus est arma Iouis fugiens et regnis exul ademptis, cum iam populus uel noui regis metu uel sua sponte depranatus deum colere desisset regemque pro deo habere coepisset, cum ipse propemodum parricida exemplo ceteris esset ad uiolandam pietatem, deseruit propere terras iustissima uirgo, sed non, ut ait Cicero, et Iouis in regno caelique in parte resedit .
reuse.text_english: But after Saturn, driven out by his son and carried to Latium, fleeing the arms of Iouis and exiled from his stolen kingdom, when now the people, either through fear of the new king or of their own accord, had been corrupted and had ceased to worship the gods and had begun to regard the king as a god, and when he himself, almost a parricide, was by his example an incitement to the rest to violate piety, the most just virgin quickly abandoned the lands; but not, as Cicero says, did she settle in the kingdom of Iouis and in part of the sky.
